_meta.title: NeuroSy-RAG medical knowledge base
_meta.note: Written for this educational project from general public-health information. Not medical advice. Symptom weights are approximate prevalence estimates used to generate synthetic training data and to score knowledge-graph coverage.

lower_right_abdominal_pain.label: lower right abdominal pain
synonyms: pain near belly button moving to the right
lower right side of my abdomen
lower right part of my stomach

dengue.name: Dengue fever
dengue.description: A mosquito-borne viral infection spread by Aedes mosquitoes, common in India during and after the monsoon. Most people recover in about a week, but a small share develop severe dengue with bleeding and plasma leakage.
precautions: Rest and drink plenty of fluids (ORS, water, coconut water).
Use paracetamol for fever; avoid aspirin and ibuprofen because they raise bleeding risk.
Use mosquito nets and repellent so the illness does not spread to others.
Get a platelet count / NS1 or dengue antibody test as advised by a doctor.
dengue.see_doctor: See a doctor within a day for a blood test if you have high fever with body or eye pain. Go to emergency care immediately for bleeding, severe abdominal pain, repeated vomiting or drowsiness, especially 3 to 7 days into the illness.

malaria.name: Malaria
malaria.description: A parasitic infection transmitted by Anopheles mosquitoes. It classically causes cycles of fever, shaking chills and heavy sweating. Plasmodium falciparum malaria can become severe quickly.
precautions: Get tested (rapid diagnostic test or blood smear) before starting treatment.
Complete the full antimalarial course prescribed by a doctor.
Sleep under insecticide-treated nets and remove standing water.
malaria.see_doctor: Any fever with chills after mosquito exposure in an endemic area needs a malaria test the same day. Confusion, breathing difficulty or jaundice are emergencies.

typhoid.name: Typhoid fever
typhoid.description: A bacterial infection caused by Salmonella Typhi, spread through contaminated food and water. Fever typically rises step by step over several days, with abdominal discomfort and weakness.
precautions: Drink only boiled or bottled water and eat freshly cooked food.
Take antibiotics only as prescribed and finish the course.
Wash hands with soap before eating and after using the toilet.
typhoid.see_doctor: A fever lasting more than 3 days, with abdominal pain or weakness, needs a doctor and a blood test (blood culture or other tests the doctor chooses).

chikungunya.name: Chikungunya
chikungunya.description: A mosquito-borne viral illness spread by Aedes mosquitoes. Its hallmark is severe, often disabling joint pain that can last weeks to months after the fever settles.
precautions: Rest, fluids and paracetamol for fever and pain.
Avoid aspirin until dengue has been ruled out.
Gentle joint movement once the fever settles; use mosquito protection.
chikungunya.see_doctor: See a doctor to confirm the diagnosis and rule out dengue, especially if you have bleeding, or if joint pain persists beyond a few weeks.

influenza.name: Influenza (flu)
influenza.description: A contagious respiratory infection caused by influenza viruses. It starts suddenly with fever, body aches and exhaustion, and is usually more severe than a common cold.
precautions: Rest, stay home and drink fluids.
Paracetamol for fever and aches.
Cover coughs and wash hands; an annual flu vaccine reduces risk.
influenza.see_doctor: Most people recover within 1 to 2 weeks. See a doctor early if you are pregnant, elderly, have a chronic illness, or develop breathing difficulty.

common_cold.name: Common cold
red_flags: high fever lasting more than 3 days
common_cold.description: A mild viral infection of the nose and throat, most often caused by rhinoviruses. It usually clears up on its own within 7 to 10 days.
precautions: Rest, warm fluids and steam inhalation.
Saline nasal drops and throat lozenges for comfort.
Antibiotics do not help a cold.
common_cold.see_doctor: See a doctor if symptoms last more than 10 days, fever is high, or you have trouble breathing.

covid19.name: COVID-19
covid19.description: An infection caused by the SARS-CoV-2 coronavirus. Symptoms range from mild cold-like illness to pneumonia. Sudden loss of smell or taste is a distinctive sign.
precautions: Test and isolate while symptomatic.
Rest, fluids and paracetamol for fever.
Monitor oxygen saturation with a pulse oximeter if available.
covid19.see_doctor: Seek care if oxygen saturation drops below 94%, breathing becomes difficult, or you are in a high-risk group.

tuberculosis.name: Pulmonary tuberculosis
tuberculosis.description: A bacterial infection by Mycobacterium tuberculosis that mainly affects the lungs and spreads through the air. India's national programme provides free testing and treatment.
precautions: Cover your mouth when coughing and keep rooms ventilated.
Get a sputum test (and chest X-ray) at a government TB centre or clinic.
If diagnosed, take every dose of the 6-month treatment.
tuberculosis.see_doctor: A cough lasting 2 weeks or more, especially with fever, night sweats or weight loss, needs a TB test.

pneumonia.name: Pneumonia
pneumonia.description: An infection that inflames the air sacs of one or both lungs, which may fill with fluid or pus. It can be caused by bacteria, viruses or fungi.
precautions: Rest semi-upright and keep hydrated.
Antibiotics only on prescription.
Monitor breathing and oxygen saturation.
pneumonia.see_doctor: Pneumonia needs a doctor's assessment. Fast breathing, low oxygen or confusion, especially in elderly people or children, needs emergency care.

bronchitis.name: Acute bronchitis
bronchitis.description: Inflammation of the airways (bronchi), usually after a cold, causing a cough that can last up to 3 weeks.
precautions: Rest, fluids, honey and warm drinks.
Avoid smoke and dust.
Antibiotics usually aren't needed for viral bronchitis.
bronchitis.see_doctor: See a doctor if the cough lasts more than 3 weeks, you cough up blood, or you become breathless.

strep_throat.name: Streptococcal pharyngitis
red_flags: drooling or unable to swallow saliva
strep_throat.description: A bacterial throat infection with sudden throat pain, fever and swollen neck glands, usually without the cough and runny nose of a cold.
precautions: Warm salt-water gargles and soft foods.
See a doctor for a throat swab; strep needs antibiotics.
Avoid sharing utensils.
strep_throat.see_doctor: See a doctor for sore throat with fever and swollen glands but no cough. Inability to swallow or breathe well is an emergency.

sinusitis.name: Acute sinusitis
sinusitis.description: Inflammation of the sinuses, usually after a cold, causing facial pain or pressure, a blocked nose and thick discharge.
precautions: Steam inhalation and saline nasal rinses.
Paracetamol for pain.
Most cases clear in 2 to 3 weeks without antibiotics.
sinusitis.see_doctor: See a doctor if symptoms last more than 10 days, are severe, or include eye swelling or vision changes.

allergic_rhinitis.name: Allergic rhinitis
allergic_rhinitis.description: An allergic reaction to airborne triggers such as dust mites, pollen or pet dander. It causes sneezing, a runny nose and itchy, watery eyes without fever.
precautions: Identify and avoid triggers (dust, pollen, smoke).
Wash bedding in hot water; keep windows closed in high-pollen seasons.
Ask a doctor or pharmacist about antihistamines or nasal sprays.
allergic_rhinitis.see_doctor: See a doctor if symptoms disturb sleep or work, or if you also wheeze.

conjunctivitis.name: Conjunctivitis
conjunctivitis.description: Inflammation of the thin membrane covering the eye ('pink eye'), caused by viruses, bacteria or allergies.
precautions: Do not rub your eyes; wash hands often.
Use a clean cloth for each eye and don't share towels.
Avoid contact lenses until it clears.
conjunctivitis.see_doctor: See an eye doctor for pain, blurred vision, or light sensitivity.

gastroenteritis.name: Acute gastroenteritis
red_flags: signs of dehydration (very little urine, dizziness)
gastroenteritis.description: Infection of the stomach and intestines, often from contaminated food or water ('stomach flu' or food poisoning). It causes diarrhoea, vomiting and cramps.
precautions: Oral rehydration solution (ORS) after each loose stool.
Small, light meals; continue breastfeeding infants.
Wash hands well and avoid preparing food for others.
gastroenteritis.see_doctor: Seek care for signs of dehydration, bloody stools, high fever, or if a child or elderly person is affected.

hepatitis_a.name: Hepatitis A
hepatitis_a.description: A viral liver infection spread through contaminated food and water. It causes jaundice (yellow skin and eyes), dark urine and tiredness, and usually resolves on its own.
precautions: Rest, fluids and a light diet.
Avoid alcohol and unnecessary medicines that strain the liver.
Practise strict hand hygiene; the vaccine prevents it.
hepatitis_a.see_doctor: Jaundice always needs a doctor and liver function tests. Confusion or bleeding is an emergency.

gerd.name: Gastro-oesophageal reflux disease
gerd.description: Stomach acid flowing back into the food pipe, causing heartburn and regurgitation, often after meals or when lying down.
precautions: Eat smaller meals; avoid lying down for 2 to 3 hours after eating.
Cut down on spicy and fatty food, caffeine, alcohol and smoking.
Raise the head of the bed.
gerd.see_doctor: See a doctor if symptoms occur more than twice a week or you have trouble swallowing. Chest pain should be checked to rule out a heart cause.

appendicitis.name: Appendicitis
appendicitis.description: Inflammation of the appendix. Pain often starts around the navel and moves to the lower right abdomen. It is a surgical emergency because the appendix can burst.
precautions: Do not eat, drink or take painkillers or laxatives until a doctor has examined you.
Do not apply heat to the abdomen.
appendicitis.see_doctor: Go to an emergency department promptly for lower right abdominal pain with fever or vomiting.

uti.name: Urinary tract infection
uti.description: A bacterial infection of the bladder or urethra. It causes burning and frequent urination, and is much more common in women.
precautions: Drink plenty of water.
Don't hold urine for long.
See a doctor for a urine test; antibiotics need a prescription.
uti.see_doctor: See a doctor within a day or two. Fever with back or side pain may mean a kidney infection and needs urgent care.

kidney_stone.name: Kidney stone (renal colic)
kidney_stone.description: Hard mineral deposits in the kidney or ureter. A moving stone causes severe, wave-like pain in the side or back that can spread to the groin.
precautions: Drink plenty of water.
Pain relief as advised by a doctor.
Strain urine to catch the stone for analysis if advised.
kidney_stone.see_doctor: Seek urgent care for severe pain, fever, or inability to pass urine.

hypertension.name: Hypertension
red_flags: BP above 180/120 with headache, chest pain, breathlessness or vision change
hypertension.description: Persistently raised blood pressure. It is often silent ('the silent killer') and is a leading risk factor for stroke and heart disease.
precautions: Check blood pressure on more than one day.
Reduce salt, stay active, keep a healthy weight, limit alcohol, stop smoking.
Take prescribed medicines regularly.
hypertension.see_doctor: Anyone with readings above 140/90 should see a doctor. Very high readings with symptoms are an emergency.

type2_diabetes.name: Type 2 diabetes
red_flags: very high blood sugar with vomiting or confusion
type2_diabetes.description: A chronic condition where the body doesn't use insulin well, causing high blood sugar. Classic signs are increased thirst, frequent urination and tiredness.
precautions: Get a fasting blood sugar or HbA1c test.
Balanced diet low in refined sugar, regular exercise, weight control.
Foot care and regular eye checks.
type2_diabetes.see_doctor: See a doctor for a blood sugar test if you have these symptoms or a family history.

hypoglycemia.name: Hypoglycaemia (low blood sugar)
hypoglycemia.description: Blood sugar dropping too low, most often in people on diabetes medicines. It causes shakiness, sweating and a racing heart, and can lead to confusion.
precautions: If conscious, take 15 g of fast sugar (glucose tablets, juice, sugar water) and recheck in 15 minutes.
Follow with a snack containing starch.
Never give food or drink to an unconscious person.
hypoglycemia.see_doctor: Repeated episodes need a review of medicines with a doctor. Unconsciousness or seizure means calling emergency services.

anemia.name: Iron-deficiency anaemia
anemia.description: A lack of healthy red blood cells, most often due to low iron. It is very common in India, especially among women, and causes tiredness, pale skin and breathlessness.
precautions: Get a haemoglobin test.
Eat iron-rich foods (greens, legumes, jaggery, meat) with vitamin C.
Take iron supplements only as advised.
anemia.see_doctor: See a doctor for a blood test if you have persistent tiredness with pale skin.

hypothyroidism.name: Hypothyroidism
hypothyroidism.description: An underactive thyroid gland that produces too little hormone, slowing metabolism and causing tiredness, weight gain and feeling cold.
precautions: Get a TSH blood test.
Take thyroid medicine on an empty stomach as prescribed.
Recheck levels as advised.
hypothyroidism.see_doctor: See a doctor for a thyroid test if these symptoms persist for weeks.

migraine.name: Migraine
red_flags: headache with fever and stiff neck
migraine.description: A primary headache disorder with recurring, often one-sided, throbbing headaches with nausea and sensitivity to light. Some people get a visual aura first.
precautions: Rest in a dark, quiet room.
Keep a headache diary to find triggers (sleep loss, skipped meals, stress).
Use pain relief early; avoid overusing painkillers.
migraine.see_doctor: See a doctor for frequent headaches. A sudden, severe or 'different' headache needs emergency care.

asthma.name: Asthma
red_flags: unable to speak in full sentences
asthma.description: A chronic condition where the airways narrow and become inflamed, causing episodes of wheezing, breathlessness and chest tightness, often triggered by allergens, cold air or exercise.
precautions: Use inhalers exactly as prescribed; carry the reliever.
Avoid known triggers like smoke and dust.
Have a written asthma action plan.
asthma.see_doctor: See a doctor for diagnosis and a treatment plan. Severe breathlessness is an emergency.

gout.name: Gout
red_flags: high fever with a hot joint (possible joint infection)
gout.description: A type of inflammatory arthritis from uric acid crystals. It causes sudden attacks of severe pain, redness and swelling, classically in the big toe.
precautions: Rest and elevate the joint; apply a cold pack.
Drink water; limit alcohol, red meat, organ meat and sugary drinks.
See a doctor about anti-inflammatory and urate-lowering treatment.
gout.see_doctor: See a doctor for a first attack. A hot joint with fever needs urgent care to rule out infection.

rheumatoid_arthritis.name: Rheumatoid arthritis
red_flags: sudden severe joint swelling with fever
rheumatoid_arthritis.description: An autoimmune disease where the immune system attacks the joint lining. It causes symmetric pain and swelling, often in the small joints of the hands, with morning stiffness lasting over 30 minutes.
precautions: See a rheumatologist early; early treatment protects joints.
Gentle exercise and physiotherapy.
Balance rest and activity.
rheumatoid_arthritis.see_doctor: See a doctor if joint pain and stiffness last more than a few weeks.

cervical_spondylosis.name: Cervical spondylosis
red_flags: loss of bladder or bowel control
cervical_spondylosis.description: Age- and posture-related wear of the discs and joints in the neck. It causes neck pain and stiffness that can spread to the shoulders and arms. It is common in people who spend long hours at desks or on phones.
precautions: Fix your posture: screen at eye level and take breaks every 30 to 45 minutes.
Do neck stretches and strengthening exercises, ideally guided by a physiotherapist.
Use a supportive pillow.
cervical_spondylosis.see_doctor: See a doctor if pain spreads into the arms with numbness or weakness.

eczema.name: Eczema (atopic dermatitis)
eczema.description: A chronic skin condition that makes skin dry, itchy and inflamed, often in skin folds. It tends to flare and settle over time.
precautions: Moisturise at least twice a day, especially after bathing.
Use mild soap-free cleansers and lukewarm water.
Avoid scratching; keep nails short.
eczema.see_doctor: See a doctor or dermatologist if itching disturbs sleep or the skin looks infected.

psoriasis.name: Psoriasis
red_flags: widespread red skin with fever or chills
psoriasis.description: An immune-mediated skin disease that causes thick, red, scaly plaques, commonly on the elbows, knees and scalp. Some people also develop joint pain (psoriatic arthritis).
precautions: Moisturise regularly.
Avoid triggers like stress, smoking and skin injury.
See a dermatologist for topical or other treatment.
psoriasis.see_doctor: See a dermatologist for diagnosis and treatment options.

chickenpox.name: Chickenpox (varicella)
chickenpox.description: A highly contagious viral infection causing an itchy rash that turns into fluid-filled blisters and then crusts over, usually with mild fever.
precautions: Stay home until all blisters have crusted.
Use calamine lotion and keep nails short.
Use paracetamol for fever; avoid aspirin in children.
chickenpox.see_doctor: See a doctor if you are an adult, pregnant or immunocompromised, or if complications appear.

panic_attack.name: Panic attack
red_flags: chest pain that could be cardiac (rule out heart attack first)
panic_attack.description: A sudden surge of intense fear with physical symptoms such as a racing heart, breathlessness and trembling. It peaks within minutes. It is frightening but not dangerous in itself.
precautions: Slow breathing (in for 4 seconds, out for 6).
Ground yourself by naming things you can see and hear.
Talk to a doctor or counsellor if attacks recur.
panic_attack.see_doctor: First-time chest pain or breathlessness should be checked medically to rule out heart or lung causes. Seek help immediately if you have thoughts of self-harm.
